title: Modèle pour End-Stage Liver maladie (Combined MELD)
abbreviations: Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (Combined MELD)
formula:
**MELD (Original, Pre-2016)** = (0.957*ln(Serum creatinine) + 0.378*ln(Serum bilirubin) + 1.120*ln(INR) + 0.643)*10

(if hemodialysis, value for Creatinine is automatically set to 4.0)

Note: If any score is <1, the MELD assumes the score is equal to 1.

**MELD Na (UNOS/OPTN):**

Per OPTN policy, January 2016 (pages 4–5):

Candidates who are at least 12 years old receive an initial MELD(i) score equal to:

MELD(i) = 0.957*ln(Creatinine) + 0.378*ln(Bilirubin) + 1.120*ln(INR) + 0.643

Then, round to the tenth decimal place and multiply by 10.

If MELD(i) > 11, perform additional MELD calculation as follows:

MELD = MELD(i) + 1.32*(137 – Na) – [0.033*MELD(i)*(137 – Na)]

**MELD 3.0:**

Candidates who are at least 18 years old at the time of registration receive an initial MELD score equal to

MELD 3.0= 1.33*(Female) + 4.56*ln(Serum bilirubin) + 0.82*(137 - Sodium) – 0.24*(137 - Sodium)*ln(Serum bilirubin) + 9.09*ln(INR) + 11.14*ln(Serum creatinine) + 1.85*(3.5 – Serum albumin) – 1.83*(3.5 – Serum albumin)*ln(Serum creatinine) + 6

Candidates who are currently at least 12 years old and were less than 18 years old at the time of registration receive a MELD score equal to:

MELD 3.0= 4.56*ln(Serum bilirubin) + 0.82*(137 - Sodium) – 0.24*(137 - Sodium)*ln(Serum bilirubin) + 9.09*ln(INR) + 11.14*ln(Serum creatinine) + 1.85*(3.5 – Serum albumin) – 1.83*(3.5 – Serum albumin)*ln(Serum creatinine) + 7.33

- Serum bilirubin, INR, and serum creatinine values below 1.0 are set to 1.0.
- Sodium is limited to a range of 125-137 mEq/L, and if outside of these bounds, is set to the nearest limit.
- Serum albumin is limited to a range of 1.5-3.5 g/dL, and if outside of these bounds, is set to the nearest limit.
- The following candidates receive a creatinine value of 3.0 mg/dL:
- The MELD 3.0 score is rounded to the nearest integer.

how_to_use.why:
- Le MELD est le score standard utilisé par l'Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network (OPTN) et détermine quels patients sont prioritaires pour recevoir une greffe de foie aux États-Unis.
- Il a été largement étudié et validé.
- L'OPTN a mis à jour son modèle MELD recommandé vers le MELD 3.0 en juin 2022.
how_to_use.when:
- Détermine le pronostic et établit la priorité pour l’accès à la transplantation hépatique.
- Si vous utilisez MELD 3.0, utilisez les éléments suivants pour guider la sélection des critères :

 - Pour les patients âgés de 12 à 18 ans, sélectionnez les critères « <18 ».
 - Pour les patients âgés de plus de 18 ans, sélectionnez les critères « ≥18 ».
- Pour les patients de moins de 12 ans, utilisez le score [PELD Cr](nabda:calc.peld-cr).
how_to_use.pearls:
- Values should be no more than 48 hours old.
- MELD can be used on any patient with end stage liver disease irrespective of cirrhosis etiology.
- Higher scores correlate with increased severity of liver dysfunction and higher three-month mortality.
- While it is mathematically possible to have a calculated MELD score >40, OPTN accepts a maximum submitted score of 40 for liver transplantation.

next_steps.advice:
- The MELD Score helps to estimate prognosis for patients with end-stage liver disease, and is used to prioritize transplant recipients.
- Consider referral to hepatologist or liver transplant center for patients with elevated MELD score.
- MELD Score should be periodically reassessed, as it changes with changing lab values.
- OPTN considers a maximum score of 40 when assessing transplant appropriateness.
- If in the United States, refer to the Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network for the latest[policies](https://optn.transplant.hrsa.gov/policies-bylaws/policies/)on liver transplant.

Interpretation:

**MELD (Original, Pre-2016) and MELD Na (UNOS/OPTN)**

| MELD Score | Mortality |
| --- | --- |
| ≤9 | 1.9% |
| 10–19 | 6.0% |
| 20–29 | 19.6% |
| 30–39 | 52.6% |
| ≥40 | 71.3% |

More Info:[OPTN/UNOS Documentation on MELD and PELD](https://optn.transplant.hrsa.gov/media/1575/policynotice_20151101.pdf)

**MELD 3.0**

Estimated 90-day survival = 0.946^exp(0.17698*MELD 3.0 – 3.56)^* 100

before_use: Sur cette page, vous trouverez le score MELD original (avant 2016), le MELD Na (anciennement standard UNOS/OPTN) et le MELD 3.0. Le MELD 3.0 est le calcul standard actuel pour l’évaluation en vue d’une transplantation d’organe aux États-Unis et tient mieux compte des disparités dans l’attribution des organes selon le sexe.
